steps.title: When prices run away
steps.body: In most of Europe, prices rise by about 2 to 3% a year. This is called [[inflation]]. In Argentina, prices rose by more than 200% in 2023. Something that cost 100 pesos in January cost about 300 pesos in December. If your money pays no interest, it then buys only a third of what it bought before.

steps.prompt: The chart shows what money with no interest can buy over the years. Move the price rise slider. Find a price rise where the money buys only half as much after 2 years.

output.label: Change in what the money can buy

steps.title: The rule of 72
steps.body: You can guess how fast prices double with the [[rule-of-72]]. Divide 72 by the price rise per year. The result is the number of years until prices double. At 3% a year, prices double in about 24 years. At 36% a year, prices double in about 2 years.

steps.prompt: Prices rise by 6% each year. About how many years does it take until prices double?
steps.explanation: 72 divided by 6 is 12. So prices double in about 12 years.

steps.prompt: True or false: if prices rise by 100% in one year, the same money buys half as much at the end of the year.
steps.explanation: True. A rise of 100% means prices double. So each peso buys half as much as before.

steps.prompt: The chart shows how much prices rose each year in Argentina. What happened in 2023?
options: Prices about tripled in one year
steps.explanation: Prices rose by about 211% in 2023. A rise of 200% means prices are three times as high. In 2024, prices still rose by about 118%.

chart.caption: Price rise in Argentina, December to December. Source: INDEC.

steps.title: Your savings and prices
steps.body: You have **{savingsBalance}** in your savings account. It pays **{savingsRate}** interest a year. When the interest is lower than the price rise, your savings buy a little less each year. The faster prices rise, the faster this happens.

steps.prompt: Your savings account pays {savingsRate} a year. Move the price rise slider. See what your savings can buy after some years.

output.label: Change in what your savings can buy

goal.hint: Move a slider to see the result change.

steps.note: The interest slider starts at your real rate. This is an example, not a forecast.
